cards.front: What should you know about molar gas volume?
cards.back: The volume occupied by one mole of any gas at room temperature and pressure (RTP). At RTP (20°C and 1 atm), one mole of any gas occupies 24 dm³ (or 24 000 cm³).

cards.front: What should you know about room temperature and pressure (rtp)?
cards.back: 20°C and 1 atmosphere pressure. At RTP, equal amounts in moles of any gas occupy the same volume.
Molar gas volume: At RTP, 1 mole of any gas occupies 24 dm³. Volume (dm³) = moles × 24. Moles = volume (dm³) ÷ 24.

Gas volume at RTP depends on the type of gas. Wrong: gas volume depends on gas type at RTP Correct: at RTP, 1 mole of ANY gas occupies 24 dm³ — the particles are far apart so particle size does not matter
6 marks: Explain how to calculate gas volumes in reactions.
A student burns 0.8 g of methane (CH₄, M r = 16) and collects the CO₂ gas produced. Equation: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O(l). The student measures 1.0 dm³ of CO₂.
